_source: Sanskrit_letters_full.docx (user-confirmed AUTHORITATIVE set, this version supersedes earlier ones)

_legend.positive: positive pole — liberating/balance (consonant) or positive acoustic essence (vowel)
_legend.negative: negative pole — binding/distortion (consonant) or negative meaning (vowel)
_legend._worldly_reference_note: Option 1 (worldly reference): the lens reads the WORLDLY (bīja) propensity of every varṇa. For a CONSONANT the worldly pole is the 'negative' field (binding vṛtti, e.g. Ka=Hope, La=Cruelty); for a VOWEL the worldly pole is the 'positive' field (active essence, e.g. a=Birth, ai=Welfare). This field asymmetry is intentional. The +/− SIGN in a reading is affirmed(+)/dissolving(−) from sound-order, NOT a field swap; the spiritual pole is the dissolved worldly one (the consonant's 'positive' counter-field).
_legend._source_corrected: Entries Ca, Ja, Ma, Ra, Va, Śa(sha), Ṣa(ssa), Sa were later corrected for Sanskrit acoustic-root source fidelity (see each entry's source_vritti/source_notes). NOTE: the NO_SIGNAL result in RESULTS_ACOUSTIC_SIGNAL.md was produced on the PRIOR lexicon; any claim about this corrected lexicon requires re-running the pre-registered signal test.

acoustic_roots: Kārya Brahma (the expressed/manifested universe; controller of the living world)
Saṃvṛtti Bodhicitta (Buddhist name for the created world)
expanded_properties.elemental: flowing water (ka = water; va = water in general)
expanded_properties.etymology: kae + ḍa = 'that which produces sound'; the roar of rivers/springs inspired the hope of survival
semantic_extensions: ka / keśa = hair grown on the head
keśa = ka + īśa = hair, also Nārāyaṇa
kāpālika = 'kaṃ saṃvṛtti bodhicittaṃ pālayati' = one who serves the living & non-living world
deity_links: Śiva (Vyomakeśa / Khakuntala — hair toward the sky; Dhurjaṭī)
expanded_properties.mantra_note: kriiṃ = ka (Kārya Brahma) + ra (luminous factor); bīja of Kālī / Bhrāmarī Tārā
expanded_properties.source_quote: Ka is the acoustic root of the abhiipśātmaka áshá vrtti. It is also the acoustic root of Kárya Brahma [the expressed universe]. … Ka (kae + d́a) etymologically means 'that which produces sound'. It also means 'water'.

acoustic_roots: the crude aspects of heaven (the transcendent sphere of heaven is kṣa)
expanded_properties.note: kha means 'sky' but is NOT the acoustic root of sky (that is ha); ka + ha = kha, so kha follows ka
expanded_properties.source_quote: The acoustic root of áshá vrtti is ka, and that of cintá vrtti [the propensity of worry] is kha. … Impersonal thoughts are symbolized by the acoustic root kha.

vrtti.name: Ceṣṭā
vrtti.english: effort / striving to arouse dormant potential

expanded_properties.note: the main cause of mundane development and spiritual elevation; acts in physical, psychic and spiritual spheres
expanded_properties.source_quote: The effort made to arouse one's dormant potentiality is called ceśt́á. … Ga, being the acoustic root of ceśt́á vrtti, plays an important role in the physical, psychic and spiritual spheres.

vrtti.name: Mamatā
vrtti.english: love / attachment (bound by time, space, individuality)

expanded_properties.imagery: the mother who sacrifices for her child yet slices kai fish without feeling; the cow who suckles then later kicks her calf — mamatā limited by relative factors; only humans can transcend it
expanded_properties.source_quote: Mamatá, the vrtti of love and attachment …, is related to time, space and individuality. … Gha is the acoustic root of mamatá vrtti.

expanded_properties.history: Vashiṣṭha is said to have learned uṋa (and the Tārā cult of Vāmācāra Tantra) from China; uṋa is used across Indo-Chinese languages
expanded_properties.source_quote: Uṋa is the acoustic root of dambha vrtti [the propensity of vanity].

ca.source_notes: Acoustic root of viveka. Negative pole Aviveka is the derived worldly distortion (source corrected from Ekāgratā/Vikṣepa).

expanded_properties.source_quote: Ca is the acoustic root of viveka [conscience].

expanded_properties.note: a mind that had been functioning properly starts malfunctioning or stops altogether
expanded_properties.source_quote: Cha is the acoustic root of vikalatáh vrtti [nervous breakdown].

ja.source_notes: Acoustic root of ahaṁkāra vṛtti. Worldly pole = ego inflation; remedial counter-pole = humility (source corrected from Dambha/vanity, which duplicated Ṅa).

expanded_properties.imagery: Aurangzeb: 'Since I was there, I controlled the situation … had I not been there the world would have met its destruction' — an expression of ahaṃkāra
expanded_properties.source_quote: Ja is the acoustic root of ahaḿkára vrtti (ego). The ego becomes inflated when one allows one's 'I' feeling to take a predominant role.

expanded_properties.etymology: Bengali nolá (greedy fascination of a cat/dog) derives from lola / lolatā
expanded_properties.source_quote: Jha is the acoustic root of lolupatá, lobha [greed] and lolatá [avarice] vrttis.

expanded_properties.note: Sanskrit pāṣaṇḍa / Hindi pākhaṇḍī = hypocrite; three forms: (1) cheating to serve one's purpose, (2) dominating to hide one's ignorance, (3) condemning sins one secretly commits
expanded_properties.source_quote: Ina is the acoustic root of kapat́atá vrtti [hypocrisy].

expanded_properties.note: NOT mere debating, and NOT kaṣāya (harsh speech to hurt); its opposite is pramita vāk (balanced, only-relevant speech). Howrah-station example.
expanded_properties.source_quote: T́a is the acoustic root of vitarka vrtti [overstating one's case]. … Vitarka is a combination of a bad temper and garrulousness.

expanded_properties.etymology: N. India paschāttāpa; anu / paschāt = 'later/after', tāpa = 'heat'
expanded_properties.source_quote: T́ha is the acoustic root of anutápa vrtti [repentance].
D́a is the acoustic root of lajjá vrtti [the propensity of shyness].

expanded_properties.imagery: slow, cruel killing (chopping legs, then tail, then head); the half-chopped live tortoise crawling away — contrary to Neohumanism
expanded_properties.source_quote: Senseless, sadistic killing is called pishunatá vrtti.
Ńa is the acoustic root of iirśá vrtti [the propensity of envy].

vrtti.name: Jāḍya / Nidrā
vrtti.english: staticity, long/deep sleep, intellectual dullness, spiritual inertness

expanded_properties.etymology: Tantra = 'taṃ jāḍyāt tārayet' (liberates from staticity); root tan = 'to expand' (taṃ vistāreṇa tārayet)
expanded_properties.source_quote: Ta is the acoustic root of staticity, long sleep and deep sleep. … That which brings about the cessation of dullness and staticity is called Tantra.
Tha is the acoustic root of viśada vrtti, of melancholy.

expanded_properties.note: speak nicely to a peevish person and they react adversely; speak harshly and they take it calmly
expanded_properties.source_quote: Da is the acoustic root of peevishness.

vrtti.name: Tṛṣṇā
vrtti.english: thirst for acquisition (wealth, name, fame, power, prestige)

expanded_properties.note: not thirst for water; cure = divert all thought toward Parama Puruṣa
expanded_properties.source_quote: Dha is the acoustic root of thirst for acquisition. This limitless craving … is called trśńa in Sanskrit.

expanded_properties.note: four types: deśagata (geo-sentiment), kālagata (time), idea-bound, ādhāragata (object); cure = ideation of indifference + Parama Puruṣa
expanded_properties.source_quote: Na is the acoustic root of moha vrtti [blind attachment or infatuation].

expanded_properties.note: one of 8 pāśas (ghṛṇā, śaṅkā, bhaya, lajjā, jugupsā, kula, śīla, māna); mainly tied to the moha ripu; root pat/patati = downward fall vs ūrdhva-gati / anurakti (devotion). The 6 ripus: kāma, krodha, lobha, mada, moha, mātsarya.
expanded_properties.source_quote: Pa is the acoustic root of ghrńá vrtti [the propensity of hatred or revulsion]. … Pa is the acoustic root of the fetter of hatred.

expanded_properties.note: generally born of more than one factor, but mainly from the moha ripu
expanded_properties.source_quote: Pha is the acoustic root of bhaya vrtti [the propensity of fear].

expanded_properties.note: distinguished from upekṣā (ignoring the truly unacceptable); related to avahelā; maitrī–karuṇā–muditā–upekṣā verse on the four attitudes
expanded_properties.source_quote: Ba is the acoustic root of avajiṋá vrtti [indifference]. … when one neglects something which may actually have some value, that is called avajiṋá.

vrtti.name: Mūrcchā
vrtti.english: deluded obsession (loss of common sense under a ripu's spell)

expanded_properties.note: NOT senselessness; cure = pratyāhāra yoga, or kīrtana / devotional song
expanded_properties.source_quote: Bha is the acoustic root of the múrcchá vrtti. … it means to lose one's common sense under the hypnotic spell of a particular ripu.

ma.source_notes: Source carries both praṇāśa and praśraya; praṇāśa added explicitly. Counter-pole Anuśāsana is the derived remedial restraint.

vrtti.name: Praṇāśa + Praśraya
vrtti.english: annihilation; and giving latitude / indulgence (Hindi baṛhvā denā)

expanded_properties.source_quote: Ma is the acoustic root of prańásha [annihilation]. It is also the acoustic root of prashraya vrtti – giving latitude [indulgence].

vrtti.name: Aviśvāsa
vrtti.english: lack of confidence (in oneself and others)

expanded_properties.elemental: constant movement (like the movement of air)
expanded_properties.note: such people say to the end 'Shall I be able to do it?' and can accomplish nothing great
expanded_properties.source_quote: Ya is the acoustic root of avishvása vrtti [lack of confidence], and is also the acoustic root of constant movement (like the movement of air).

ra.source_notes: Corrected: agnitattva/fire moved to the positive (vitality) pole; only Sarvanāśa (destructive annihilation-thought) remains negative.

vrtti.name: Agnitattva / Prāṇaśakti (vitality) + Sarvanāśa (annihilation-thought)
vrtti.english: vitality / fire; and the defeatist thought 'everything is gone, I am undone'

expanded_properties.note: sarvanāśa cured by guru mantra auto-suggestion 'Parama Puruṣa is mine / I am destined to win'
expanded_properties.mantra_note: Raṃ bījaṃ shikhinaṃ dhyāyet, trikoṇam-aruṇaprabham (meditate on the bīja Raṃ, triangular, fire-red)
expanded_properties.source_quote: Ra is the acoustic root of agnitattva or práńashakti – vitality. … It is also the acoustic root of sarvanásha [the thought of annihilation]. … the monosyllabic word ra means 'fire'.

expanded_properties.mantra_note: Laṃ bījaṃ dharaṇīṃ dhyāyet, caturāsrāṃ supītābhām (meditate on bīja Laṃ, square, golden — the earth factor)
expanded_properties.source_quote: La is the acoustic root of kruratá vrtti [cruelty]. … La is also the acoustic root of kśititattva, the solid factor.

va.positive: Dharma / Jalatattva (original stance, sustaining righteousness / liquid coherence)
va.negative: Adharma (deviation from original stance / loss of sustaining order)
va.source_vritti: Dharma (ensconcement in original stance) + Jalatattva (liquid / water factor)
va.source_notes: Corrected: Dharma is the sustaining (positive) pole, NOT a binding pole; worldly distortion = Adharma. Satya removed (was prior positive).

vrtti.name: Dharma
vrtti.english: ensconcement in one's original stance; movement toward Parama Puruṣa

expanded_properties.elemental: jalatattva (the liquid factor — any liquid, not only water)
expanded_properties.note: Dhriyate dharma ityāhuḥ — 'dharma is that which sustains'; humanity cannot sprout except in the soil of dharma
expanded_properties.source_quote: Va is the acoustic root of dharma. … Va is also the acoustic root of jalatattva [the liquid factor], and the acoustic root of the rain-god Varuńa Deva.

sha.positive: Directed energy / purposeful material pursuit (dynamic accomplishment)
sha.source_notes: Greed is the distorted form, not the whole source; positive pole = purposeful dynamic accomplishment (rajasic energy).

vrtti.name: Rajoguṇa + Artha
vrtti.english: the mutative principle; and artha (psychic longing — temporary cessation of worldly wants)

expanded_properties.note: shra = mutative principle + vitality (ra); shra + ṅīṣ = shrii (hence 'Śrī' before a name, a blessing on dynamism)
expanded_properties.source_quote: Sha is the acoustic root of rajoguńa [the mutative principle]. It is also the acoustic root of artha [psychic longing].

ssa.source_notes: Worldly pole = kāma / tamoguṇa; counter-pole = transmutation of desire. Source alignment made explicit.

vrtti.name: Tamoguṇa + Kāma
vrtti.english: the static principle; and kāma (all physical/worldly desires — wealth, fame, position)

expanded_properties.note: one of the four vargas (dharma=va, artha=sha, kāma=ṣa, mokṣa=sa)
expanded_properties.source_quote: Śa is the acoustic root of tamoguńa [the static principle], and is also the acoustic root of all kinds of worldly desires … káma.

sa.source_notes: Liberation / sattva is the source root (positive); negative pole = escapist / static withdrawal.

expanded_properties.note: completes the four vargas: va=dharma, sha=artha, ṣa=kāma, sa=mokṣa; and the three guṇas: sha=rajas, ṣa=tamas, sa=sattva
expanded_properties.source_quote: Sa is the acoustic root of mokśa [salvation, unqualified liberation]. … sa is the acoustic root of sattvaguńa [the sentient principle].

vrtti.name: Parā-vidyā
vrtti.english: intuitional science; ethereal factor, daytime, the sun, svarloka

expanded_properties.note: opposite of ṭha (night, moon, bhūvarloka, kāmamaya kośa); ha + ao = hao (Śiva in tāṇḍava dance); Śiva as preceptor = aeṃ (also bīja of the guru and of Sarasvatī)
expanded_properties.source_quote: Ha is the acoustic root of the ethereal factor, of daytime, of the sun, of svarloka, and of parávidyá [intuitional science].

expanded_properties.note: also the acoustic root of the transcendent sphere of heaven (vs kha = crude heaven)
expanded_properties.source_quote: Kśa is the acoustic root of mundane knowledge, and is also the acoustic root of material science.

u.negative: tunnel vision, missing the whole picture

am.negative: purging without integration, loss of vital essence

contextual_usage.word_start: consonant acts more strongly in its assertive projection (outer call)
contextual_usage.word_middle: consonant often takes relational / softening roles, blending into neighbors
contextual_usage.word_end: consonant acts as closure / return signal (anchoring the energy)
